market_context: United States; selecting mature watermelon at retail.
title: How to Choose a Ripe, Sweet Watermelon

seo.title: How to Choose a Ripe, Sweet Watermelon
seo.meta_description: Look for a creamy-yellow ground spot, good weight for size, and sound rind. Watermelon does not gain much sugar after harvest, so it must be picked mature.
seo.search_intent: Choose a watermelon that has already reached good maturity and sweetness.

excerpt: One of the best clues is the ground spot. As watermelon reaches harvest maturity, the area resting on the soil changes from pale white to cream or yellow. The melon should also feel heavy for its size and have no deep cracks or soft, decaying areas. It will not become meaningfully sweeter after harvest.
content_html:
Thumping a watermelon and listening for a perfect hollow sound is traditional, but maturity is better judged by several physical clues together.

The ground spot is useful

UC Davis notes that the portion of the melon resting on the soil changes from pale white to creamy yellow at proper harvest maturity. A completely white spot can suggest earlier harvest.

Heavy for its size

A well-hydrated watermelon should feel substantial compared with another melon of similar size. You do not need a scale; compare two similar fruits.

Inspect the rind

Avoid deep cracks, wet decay, leaking, or large soft bruises. Superficial scarring is less important than structural damage.

It will not sweeten much at home

Watermelon is non-climacteric. UC Davis notes that internal color and sugar do not meaningfully increase after the fruit is removed from the vine. Waiting several days cannot fix an immature watermelon.

What about the sound?

It can provide some information about internal structure, but sound varies with cultivar, size, and the listener’s experience. Use it only as a supporting clue.

Creamy-yellow ground spot, good weight, sound rind, and no soft decay are more useful together than any single trick.

faq.question: Does watermelon ripen after you buy it?
faq.answer: Not in the same way as bananas or mangoes. It does not become much sweeter after harvest.

faq.question: Is a yellow ground spot a good sign?
faq.answer: Yes. Creamy-yellow color where the melon rested on the soil is a recognized maturity indicator.

faq.question: Should watermelon sound hollow?
faq.answer: Sound can be a supporting clue, but it is not reliable enough to use alone.
